# Daymark

> Daymark keeps one person's commitments across agent sessions. Plans, deadlines, earliest starts and hoped-for finishes carry different meanings. An agent can recover a handoff, propose work for a person to decide on, and adapt advice to a request. The core uses SQLite and Python 3.11 or newer.

Check `daymark --version`. The tagged source release is 0.6.0. For the guide that matches your installed CLI, run `daymark onboard --skill`.

## Start here

- [Agent guide](agents.md) covers first use, dates, reading, writing, errors and safe retries.
- [Tagged 0.6.0 agent guide](https://github.com/lavallee/daymark/blob/v0.6.0/docs/agents.md) matches the release install.
- [MCP clients](mcp.md) covers a read-only first connection, scoped pickup, structured results and recovery after a lost reply.
- [Review a Todoist CSV](todoist-csv.md) covers same-title rows, schedules and confirmed source links.
- [Working with a person's preferences](working-preferences.md) covers one answer, a standing workspace choice and a personal choice that expires.
- [Work and life](work-and-life.md) shows how Daymark can work beside Beads, Things and Todoist.
- [Operations](operations.md) covers authenticated HTTP, recording reminders, transfers and restoring a backup.
- [Architecture](architecture.md) and [strategy extensions](strategy-plugins.md) explain which facts belong in the engine and how a host can supply another way of working.

## Evidence and source

- [Agent journeys](research/agent-journeys.md) includes a reproducible synthetic client evaluation.
- [MCP trials](research/mcp-client-trials.md) records the actual clients, outcomes and limits.
- [Project source and installation](https://github.com/lavallee/daymark) provides the README and release tags.
